column1: # Bundle sjl-9-001: every group of Broiler.VM's divergences files for the Intl reference datasets, each
# with its class for part C of this bundle's decision rule (milestone SJL-9, work package SJL-9.1, task
# Each file is read from that commit's objects; `blob` is the file's Git blob id there, so
# Files: src/tests/cldr/<area>/divergences.txt for every area that has one (orderings has none), and the
# divergences of the Temporal Intl programs under src/tests/temporal/ (intl, calendars-intl, zone-names).
# A GROUP is a run of comment lines, its header, and the run of divergence lines right under it; a blank
# line ends it. Each file's first comment run, which no divergence line follows, is the file's own
# preamble and no group. Every divergence line of these files falls in exactly one group, as a check
# run when this table was written found. `lines` is the group from its header's first line
# to its last divergence line; `header-lines` and `divergence-lines` are its two parts, counted from the
# file's first line; `divergences` is how many divergence lines it holds. `header` quotes the header
# whole, its `# ` markers removed and its lines joined by a space.
# CLASSES. A reviewer reads each header against them.
# - spec: both engines owe the line Broiler.VM writes, by the pinned text (ECMA-402 at decision D14's
#   pin, with Intl over Temporal by tc39/proposal-temporal@e8cc03fc), by the data both engines carry
#   (CLDR 48.2.0, tzdb 2026e), or by a choice the shared code makes; Broiler.JS's line after its
#   cut-over equals Broiler.VM's, and part C fails a line of a spec group that differs from it.
# - coverage: the line is Broiler.VM's for want of a locale, a calendar or a tailoring its data lacks
#   (decision D5), or, for the durations group the note names, a numbering system's symbols (decision
#   D21); Broiler.JS answers from its own data, and part C's class V admits its line when it equals the
#   retained answer (class R when it equals the CLDR 48 reference's).
# - zone: row Z8, the time-zone identifier a formatter resolves (decision D15); part C's class Z8.
# `note` says why, in a few words.

column8: note
column9: header

column8: U+202F in the string; CLDR's character, which decision D25 makes a data change (C5) for Broiler.JS
column9: Node's format writes U+0020 where ICU writes U+202F: V8 replaces ICU's narrow no-break space by a space in the string format, the Date toLocale methods and a range of practically equal dates answer, and not in the parts formatToParts and formatRangeToParts answer. ECMA-402 (the current draft, 11.5.7 FormatDateTime and 11.5.10 FormatDateTimeRange) makes each string the concatenation of the parts the ToParts form answers, so the profile writes ICU's character in both. Only the string differs on these lines; the parts are ICU's.

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: CLDR 48 writes the German flexible day period with the hour as "h 'Uhr' B": CLDR 47, which ICU 77.1 carries, writes availableFormats Bh as "h B", and the profile carries CLDR 48.2. The pattern is CLDR's data, not ECMA-402's; the range of two hours apart, written by the interval format, is the same in both releases.

column8: ECMA-402 reports the fields the format has
column9: V8 reads the letters of a quoted literal as fields: the era and month format with no year has the pattern "G ('month': LLL)" in both, and Node's resolvedOptions reports an hour and a minute from the quoted word. ECMA-402 (11.3.2) reports the fields the format has, which are the era and the month.

column8: ECMA-402 regularizes the code's case
column9: ECMA-402 regularizes a code's case before it names it (12.5.1 CanonicalCodeForDisplayNames): a region is uppercased, a script title-cased and a calendar lowercased, so `us`, `latn` and `GREGORY` are named as `US`, `Latn` and `gregory` are. V8 hands ICU the code as written, which names none of them.

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: CLDR 48 renamed three calendars these locales name: English's `iso8601` is "Gregorian Calendar (ISO 8601 Weeks)", where CLDR 47 had "ISO-8601 Calendar", and German's tabular and Umm al-Qura Hijri calendars are "Hidschra-Kalender (...)", where CLDR 47 had "Bürgerlicher Hidschri-Kalender (tabellarisch)" and "Hidschri-Kalender (Umm al-Qura)". Node 22.22.0 carries CLDR 47.

column8: CLDR's names, which both engines carry
column9: ICU names two language codes otherwise than CLDR's data does. It joins a code's variants into one key, so `sl-rozaj-biske` finds no name and is written "BISKE_ROZAJ", or nothing under the none fallback; the profile names each variant from CLDR's variants. And it names `und` "root", its own name for the root locale, where CLDR's languages name it "Unknown language".

column8: ECMA-402 throws a RangeError
column9: An empty script code cannot be matched by unicode_script_subtag, so it is a RangeError (12.5.1 CanonicalCodeForDisplayNames, step 3.a). V8 returns the empty string.

column8: the current draft's DurationFormat
column9: Node 22's DurationFormat predates the current draft (13 DurationFormat Objects) in seven ways, and each line below shows one or more of them. In the draft: - only the first unit written carries the sign; every later unit is formatted with signDisplay 'never' (13.5.15 PartitionDurationFormatPattern, 13.5.12 FormatNumericUnits), and a negative duration's first unit is -0 where its value is 0; - a clock (numeric or 2-digit units) is one element of the unit list, so a written unit before it is followed by the list's separator, not by a time separator (13.5.15, 13.5.14 ListFormatParts); - seconds after numeric minutes are 2-digit and displayed always, so 5 minutes is 5:00 (13.5.6 GetDurationUnitOptions); - a clock's numbers are not grouped, useGrouping false (13.5.9 to 13.5.11); - fractions are truncated, roundingMode 'trunc', so 7.008 seconds to two digits is 7.00 (13.5.11, 13.5.15); - a fractional unit displayed 'always', and a word style after a numeric unit, are RangeErrors (13.5.6.2 ValidateDurationUnitStyle), and years of 2^32 or more are a RangeError (13.5.5 IsValidDuration); - resolvedOptions writes numberingSystem second, after locale (13.3.2, table 21).

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: CLDR 48 changed two of German's narrow duration patterns: the hour from '{0} Std.' to '{0}h', and the millisecond's singular to '{0}ms'. CLDR 47, ICU 77.1's, has the old ones. This was found by reading both releases' units.json for de. Some lines here also show the sign of the first group.

column8: a numbering system's own symbols, which Broiler.VM's data lacks and Broiler.JS's carries (decision D21); not a locale, calendar or tailoring
column9: The profile writes a numbering system other than latn with the language's latn symbols (JSD-0044 section 5), where ICU writes arab's own grouping separator and its letter mark before the minus. These lines also show the sign of the first group.

column8: Temporal's amendment, which both engines follow (JSD-0078 decision D1)
column9: The profile admits Temporal (JSD-0054), and the proposal amends format and formatToParts to read their argument with ToTemporalDuration, which takes an ISO 8601 duration string; Node 22 does not, and throws for a string as ECMA-402 alone says.

column8: ECMA-402 makes a part for every element
column9: ICU reports no part for an empty element, so Node joins the literals around it into one. ECMA-402 (the current draft, 14.5.2 CreatePartsFromList and 14.5.1 DeconstructPattern) makes a part of type element for every element of the list, its value the empty String where the element is empty, and places it between the literals of its pattern. Both join to the same string.

column8: the draft's firstDayOfWeek
column9: Node 22 predates the draft's firstDayOfWeek: its V8 reads neither the option nor the -u-fw keyword into the property, and does not let it set the week's first day. ECMA-402 (the current draft, 15.1.1 Intl.Locale, 15.3.6 firstDayOfWeek and 15.5.17 WeekInfoOfLocale) reads the option as WeekdayToUValue states, keeps the keyword, and makes it the first day.

column8: the draft's variants
column9: Node 22 predates the draft's variants: its V8 has no variants property and ignores the option. ECMA-402 (15.1.2 UpdateLanguageId, 15.3.23 variants) reads the option into the tag, and the property answers the canonical tag's variants, sorted as canonicalization sorts them.

column8: ECMA-402's language of und
column9: Node 22's language property is undefined for the language und. ECMA-402 (15.3.8 language, 15.5.2 GetLocaleLanguage) answers the first subtag, und.

column8: calendar: Broiler.VM formats the Gregorian calendar alone (JSD-0045)
column9: The profile formats the Gregorian calendar alone (JSD-0045). ECMA-402 (15.5.9 CalendarsOfLocale) keeps of a region's calendars in use those AvailableCalendars has, so the profile answers gregory where Node, whose ICU formats them all, lists the region's others too.

column8: tailoring: Broiler.VM's Collator offers phonebk for German only (JSD-0043)
column9: The profile's Collator offers phonebk for German and no other tailoring (JSD-0043). ECMA-402 (15.5.10 CollationsOfLocale) answers the collator's own collations for a locale it supports, and emoji and eor for one it does not, so the profile answers those where Node lists ICU's.

column8: a region's zones from tzdb 2026e's zone.tab, which both engines carry; not the formatter's resolved zone (row Z8)
column9: A region's time zones are tzdb 2026e's zone.tab entries for it (JSD-0053), which are IANA Zone names, as ECMA-402 (15.5.13 TimeZonesOfLocale) asks. Node 22 answers CLDR's older canonical names where they differ: America/Indianapolis for America/Indiana/Indianapolis, America/Coral_Harbour for America/Atikokan.

column8: ECMA-402's hour cycles from CLDR's time data
column9: ECMA-402 (15.5.11 HourCyclesOfLocale) answers the hour cycles in common use in the region, most preferred first; the profile reads them from CLDR's time data, the preferred cycle and then the allowed ones. Node 22 answers only the preferred cycle.

column8: locale: Broiler.VM's NumberFormat supports German and English only
column9: The profile's NumberFormat supports German and English only. ECMA-402 (15.5.12 NumberingSystemsOfLocale) answers latn for a locale it does not support, where Node answers the locale's default numbering system.

column8: ECMA-402's PartitionNumberRangePattern
column9: ICU's range spans for a currency code: ICU 77.1 places the spans of the two numbers before it inserts the currency spacing, so every source after the space is shifted by one character (`fraction/shared`, `literal/endRange` for the separator). ECMA-402's PartitionNumberRangePattern gives each number's parts its own source and the separator `shared`, which is what is written here.

column8: ECMA-402's FormatApproximately
column9: ICU's approximate percent range: formatRange(1, 1) under style percent answers `~10,000%` in ICU 77.1, the value multiplied by 100 twice on the approximately path. ECMA-402's FormatApproximately writes the formatted number with an approximately sign, `~100%`, which is what is written here.

column8: ECMA-402's ToIntlMathematicalValue
column9: A string too small to be a Number: ECMA-402's ToIntlMathematicalValue (step 9, RoundMVResult) answers 0 for "1e-400", as its Number would be +0. Node 22.22.0 keeps the exact value. The answers written here are those of 0 under each case's options.

column8: ECMA-402's range identity
column9: The range's identity is ECMA-402's: PartitionNumberRangePattern writes a range approximately when FormatNumeric(x) is FormatNumeric(y), and with signDisplay never -1 and 1 both format as `1`. ICU 77.1 compares the values and writes `1-1`.

column8: ECMA-402's ToIntlMathematicalValue takes a BigInt
column9: Node 22's select converts its argument with ToNumber, so a BigInt is a TypeError. ECMA-402 (the current draft, 17.3.3 Intl.PluralRules.prototype.select) converts it with ToIntlMathematicalValue, which takes a BigInt as its exact value.

column8: ECMA-402's ResolvePluralRange
column9: ICU 77.1 resolves every range by CLDR's plural ranges, which name no range from one to one, so it answers other. ECMA-402 (17.5.4 ResolvePluralRange) answers the start's category when both ends write the same string under FormatNumericToString, whose string has no sign: 1 and 1.0001 under three fraction digits, -1 and 1, and 0.5 and 1 rounded to no fraction digits are each one string.

column8: the draft's notation option
column9: Node 22 predates the draft's notation option: its V8 neither reads it nor applies the compact rounding SetNumberFormatDigitOptions gives it. ECMA-402 (17.1.1 Intl.PluralRules, 16.1.2 SetNumberFormatDigitOptions) rounds a compact notation to two significant digits and no fraction digits, so 0.999 and 1.004 are 1.

column8: the draft's resolvedOptions; the header's third way, en-US and de-DE resolving to themselves, is an available-locale policy that Broiler.JS's host availability (decision D7) answers alike
column9: Each resolvedOptions differs from Node 22's in up to three ways. Node predates the draft's notation and compactDisplay properties (17.3.2, table 32), which the profile writes. ICU lists the plural categories in its rules' order, where the draft sorts them zero, one, two, few, many, other. And V8's PluralRules is available only for languages, so en-US and de-DE resolve to en and de, where the profile's available locales are the same four for every constructor (JSD-0043).

column8: ECMA-402 looks the literal up by ToString(value)
column9: Under numeric 'auto', ICU rounds the value as its number format would, finds 0, and writes CLDR's literal for 0 ('today', 'jetzt'). ECMA-402 (the current draft, 18.5.2 PartitionRelativeTimePattern) looks the literal up by ToString(value), which for 0.0001 is '0.0001'. CLDR names no literal for it, so the value is written with its pattern, its number rounded to 0.

column8: UAX #29's default word rules, which both engines apply through Broiler.Unicode since SJL-7; part C reads segments.js's lines as class O
column9: ICU segments ideographic text into words by a dictionary of Chinese and Japanese words, so it keeps U+65E5 U+672C U+8A9E ('Japanese') together. The profile carries no dictionary and applies UAX #29's default word rules, under which an ideograph's Word_Break is Other and every ideograph is a word of its own (WB999). ECMA-402 (the current draft, 19.8.1 FindBoundary) leaves the boundaries to the implementation and names UAX #29's default algorithms. Each such segment is still word-like.

column8: row Z8: a line keyed by an identifier that is not its own primary moves at SJL-9.4 (decision D15); a line keyed by a primary resolves to itself in both engines and stays
column9: ECMA-402 6.5 makes every Zone of the IANA Time Zone Database a primary identifier and resolves a Link to its Zone, by CLDR's grouping where the note recommends it, and Intl.DateTimeFormat resolves a name to its primary identifier (11.1.2 step 36). CLDR's time zone keys name that Zone in their `_iana` attribute: Asia/Kolkata for Asia/Calcutta, Europe/Kyiv for Europe/Kiev. V8 in Node 22.22.0 answers CLDR's own canonical identifier instead, the key's first alias, which is the older name. The offsets agree on every one of these lines.

column8: tzdb 2026e, which both engines carry since SJL-8
column9: Morocco moved to permanent +00 on 2026-09-20, which tzdb 2026e records and its NEWS states; Node 22.22.0 carries tzdb 2025b, which predicts Morocco's Ramadan changes to 2087 and +01 after them. So 2150 is +00 here, for Casablanca and for Western Sahara's El Aaiun, which follows Morocco.

column8: the identifiers Intl lists (TimeZonesOfLocale, supportedValuesOf); not the formatter's resolved zone (row Z8)
column9: The same resolution, in the lists: a region's zones are zone.tab's, which are IANA Zone names (15.5.13 TimeZonesOfLocale asks for canonical Zone names), and the identifiers Intl lists are the primary ones (6.5.3), so Asia/Kolkata, Europe/Kyiv and America/Indiana/Indianapolis where V8 lists CLDR's older names. V8 also leaves UTC and the 26 Etc/GMT offset zones out of the list, though each is a primary identifier.

column8: U+202F, as the dates group
column9: Node writes U+0020 where ICU writes U+202F: V8 replaces ICU's narrow no-break space before a day period by a space, as the dates dataset under src/tests/cldr/dates names; the profile writes CLDR's U+202F (74 lines).

column8: the draft's AdjustDateTimeStyleFormat, not the polyfill's fixed options
column9: The polyfill fakes dateStyle for a year-month or a month-day with fixed options (its dateStyleHacks: short is year 2-digit and month numeric, medium month short). The draft's AdjustDateTimeStyleFormat (amended ECMA-402 s15.6.2) keeps the style pattern's own fields and widths, which the profile follows (6 lines).

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: CLDR 48 adds the available format GyM, 'M/y G' in English and 'MM/y G' in German, which CLDR 47 lacks; ICU 77.1 matches the skeleton to GyMMM instead (2 lines).

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: 1. CLDR 48 names eras that CLDR 47 leaves as placeholders or abbreviates: the Coptic and Ethiopian eras, ERA0 and ERA1 in CLDR 47, are AA, AM and Anno Martyrum in CLDR 48; the Indian era Saka is Śaka; and English's long name of the Hijri era, AH in CLDR 47, is Anno Hegirae. Each line differs from the polyfill's in the era name alone, which is the archived CLDR 48 data's (1386 lines).

column8: CLDR's resolved data
column9: 2. German's date-time glue in the Chinese and Korean calendars: CLDR's resolved data, 47's as 48's, gives '{1} {0}'; ICU 77.1 writes the generic calendar's '{1}, {0}'. The profile writes CLDR's (2).

column8: the polyfill's rebuilt formatter drops the year; a formatter keeps it
column9: 3. The polyfill formats a plain date-time through a formatter it rebuilds from resolvedOptions(), which ICU gives no year for the Chinese and Korean calendars, so it drops the year a Date formatted with the same options keeps (Node writes "Mo4 16, 2024, 08:30" for it); the German lines also take the glue of group 2 (4).

column8: implementation-defined; the shared calendar code's fallback (SJL-10), which both engines take
column9: 4. The deprecated Hijri calendars: the proposal's CreateDateTimeFormat, as test262 states it, leaves it to the implementation which available calendar "islamic-rgsa" falls back to; the profile's is "islamic-tbla", as for "islamic", and ICU's "islamic-umalqura". The proposal's AvailableCalendars is Table 1's calendars, which lists neither "islamic" nor "islamic-rgsa" (3).

column8: U+202F, as the dates group
column9: 1. Node writes U+0020 where ICU writes U+202F: V8 replaces ICU's narrow no-break space before a day period by a space, as the dates dataset under src/tests/cldr/dates names; the profile writes CLDR's U+202F (17 lines).

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: 2. CLDR 48 changes which metazone a zone uses when, or a metazone's golden zone: Russia's regional zones, Istanbul, Famagusta, the Caucasus and Central Asia, Monrovia and Palmer take another metazone or none, and the Hawaii-Aleutian metazone's golden zone is America/Adak, Pacific/Honolulu having a Hawaii metazone of its own (59 lines).

column8: CLDR 48 data, which both engines carry
column9: 3. CLDR 48 renames metazones and exemplar cities: West Africa has one name, West Africa Time, where CLDR 47 gave a generic, a standard and a daylight one; Hovd is Khovd, Qyzylorda Kyzylorda, Ponape Pohnpei; and cities take their own spelling or full name (São Paulo, Córdoba, Ürümqi, Aktau, the Antarctic stations, the Pacific islands and atolls) (199 lines).
